He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke Blue Devils]]. As a high school senior, Trent Jr. was selected as an [[2017 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|McDonald's All-American]].{{cite web | url = http://www.maxpreps.com/news/-c4H_udHpk68Wy2LGvrS3Q/2017-mcdonald’s-all-american-game-boys-rosters-announced.htm | title = 2017 McDonald’s All-American Game boys rosters announced | work = maxpreps | date = 15 January 2017 | accessdate = 20 February 2017}} ==Early life== Gary is the son of [[Gary Trent]], an American retired professional basketball player. He has three brothers named Garyson, Grayson and Graydon. Gary's father, Gary Trent Sr., played on the 1993 U.S. Olympic Festival North Team that finished with a 4-0 record and captured the gold medal. He also played basketball at Ohio University, nine years in the NBA for the [[Portland Trail Blazers]], [[Toronto Raptors]], [[Dallas Mavericks]] and [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] and also competed in Greece and Italy.https://www.usab.com/basketball/players/mens/t/trent-jr-gary-1.aspx ===Recruiting=== Trent Jr. was considered one of the best players in the 2017 recruiting class by [[Scout.com]], [[Rivals.com]] and [[ESPN]].[https://247sports.com/Player/Gary-Trent-Jr-38115]http://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/190305/gary-trent-jr On November 10, 2016 Gary committed to the Duke Blue Devils. Trent Jr. signed his letter of intent on the same day. {{College athlete recruit start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2017}} {{College athlete recruit entry | recruit = Gary Trent Jr. | position = SG | hometown = [[Napa, California|Napa, CA]] | highschool = Prolific Prep (CA) | feet = 6 | inches = 5 | weight = 213 | 40 = | commitdate = November 10, 2016 | scout stars = 5 | rivals stars = 5 | 247 stars = 5 | espn stars = 5 | espn grade = 95 }} {{College athlete recruit end | 40 = | year = 2017 | rivals ref title = Duke 2017 Basketball Commitments | scout ref title = 2017 Duke Basketball Commits | espn ref title = 2017 Duke Blue Devils Recruiting Class | 247 ref title = 2017 Duke 24/7 Sports Commits | rivals school = Duke | 247 school = Duke | scout s = Duke | espn schoolid = | scout overall = #12 | rivals overall = #13 | 247 overall = #10 | espn overall = #8 | accessdate = September 6, 2016 | bball = yes }} ==College career== On November 10, 2016, Trent Jr. committed to the Duke Blue Devils, he signed his letter of intent on the same day.{{cite web|last1=Solari|first1=Chris|title=Michigan State basketball target Gary Trent Jr. picks Duke|url=http://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/michigan-state/spartans/2016/11/10/michigan-state-basketball-gary-trent-jr/93621550/|website=Detroit Free Press|accessdate=August 22, 2017|date=November 10, 2016}} On January 13, 2018, despite battling an illness, Trent scored 19 points to beat [[Wake Forest Demon Deacons men's basketball|Wake Forest]]. Against [[Miami Hurricanes men's basketball|Miami]] on January 15, Trent scored a career-high 30 points in a Duke comeback victory.{{cite news|last1=Alexander|first1=Jonathan|title=If there’s one thing for certain, it’s that Duke’s Gary Trent Jr. has shown he is clutch|url=http://www.newsobserver.com/sports/college/acc/duke/duke-now/article195615694.html|accessdate=January 24, 2018|work=The News & Observer|date=January 19, 2018}} Following Duke's loss in the [[2018 NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Tournament|2018 NCAA Men's Basketball Tournament]], Trent announced his intention to forgo his final three seasons of collegiate eligibility and declare for the [[2018 NBA Draft]], where he is expected to be a first round selection.{{Cite news|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2018/04/07/gary-trent-jr-leaving-duke-after-1-season-for-nba-draft/33633919/|title=Gary Trent Jr. leaving Duke for NBA draft|work=[[USA Today]]|date=April 7, 2018}} ===College statistics=== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"| [[2017–18 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2017–18]] | style="text-align:left;"| [[2017–18 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team|Duke]] | 37 || 37 || 33.8 || .415 || .402 || .876 || 4.2 || 1.4 || 1.2 || .2 || 14.5 {{S-end}} ==References== {{reflist}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Trent, Gary Jr.}} [[Category:1999 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:American men's basketball players]] [[Category:Duke Blue Devils men's basketball players]] [[Category:McDonald's High School All-Americans]] [[Category:Shooting guards]] [[Category:Sportspeople from Columbus, Ohio]] {{US-basketball-bio-stub}}
